thread:
romy: Heads-up: landing SFO ~00:40 then connecting to SEA at 08:15. Looking for low-key spots to charge, nap, and maybe shower. Any SFO veterans here?
diego: Gate G/near the SkyTerrace is usually chill late, less foot traffic. Also lots of outlets by the seating clusters.
sophie: If you have access, the United Club near G gates opens late and has power + snacks. Otherwise, the Centurion lounge in Terminal 3 has showers but it's hit-or-miss.
ellie: Pro-tip: the airport has a quiet family restroom area with bench-like seating near T2 — unpopular spot, so fewer people. Also tuck your bag under the bench.
romy: Is the airside connector between T2 and T3 open overnight? Trying to avoid re-clearing security.
diego: Usually yes, but depends on maintenance. Allow 30-45m to move between terminals if you need to. Keep boarding pass handy.
sophie: For showers: Minute Suites aren't at SFO AFAIK. Marriott Gateway has a day-use option but it's outside the secure zone. If you want inside, hunt for lounges that sell day passes.
ellie: Food recs for late night: a small bento or yogurt + granola, avoid spicy stuff if you want to nap. Bring a refillable bottle to use the water stations.
romy: Packing list I'm following:
```
- short USB-C cable
- 20k mAh battery pack
- eye mask + earplugs
- small snacks (nuts, bars)
- hoodie/scarf
```
diego: That looks perfect. One extra: a tiny padlock for a locker if you stash stuff, and a printed boarding pass backup in case phone dies.
airportbot: Charging map + lounge hours: https://flysfo.com/en/airport-guide/terminals-and-gates/charging-stations
sophie: If anyone wants to trade a lounge guest pass for stickers, I have one from a recent conference. DM me :grimacing:
romy: Legend. I'll bring extra stickers for whoever helps me score coffee at 4am :coffee: Safe travels, all!
